messages:
Laura: quick proposal: introduce a lease-based GC for on-prem artifact stores + signed tombstone provenance for evicted blobs.
Laura: motivation: long-lived air-gapped clusters accumulate bundle/image history and hit disk pressure. We need safe eviction that preserves auditability and resume semantics.
Raj: question: eviction triggers? retention_count per-component vs global TTL?
Laura: policy model = per-component retention_count + cluster-wide TTL. Evict writes a signed tombstone file that records provenance, not just delete. Manifest graph can be trimmed but provenance anchors remain.
Tim: agent resume concern: if a blob is evicted and a node tries to resume, do we fail hard?
Laura: agent consults local tombstone index. If blob missing and tombstoned => return resumable=false + operator guidance. If not tombstoned and missing => hard error.
Maya: audit/signing: tombstone must include signing root, activation epoch, and a compact proof anchor so audits can attest that a now-evicted blob was once active.
Laura: example tombstone (proposal):
```
{
  "artifact": "component/foo@sha256:abcd...",
  "evicted_at": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z",
  "reason": "retention_count_exceeded",
  "signed_by": "operator-key:v3",
  "proof_anchor": "anchor-sha256:fff..."
}
```
Raj: +1 for compact anchor. Perf: scanning a global tombstone index worries me.
Laura: plan: sharded local tombstone indexes per node, local lease TTL (default 30d), and a periodic cluster compaction window. Eviction only proceeds when local lease expired AND cluster quorum agrees (prevents split-brain double eviction).
Tim: ops flow: who can rehydrate if customer needs an old version?
Laura: `redwoodctl artifacts fetch --rehydrate <id>` will attempt peer-fastpull, then fallback to prompting for archival seed restore. If neither available the CLI surfaces the signed tombstone for SRE-approved restore.
Maya: registry compatibility: some on-prem registries expect OCI manifests. Make tombstone consumable via OCI manifest annotations (e.g., `com.redwood.tombstone=1`) and as a sibling object. No registry behavior change.
OperatorBot: lint: tombstone-schema v1 validated against spec/tombstone-schema.yaml \u2705
Raj: recovery/rollback: what if operator needs an immediate rollback to an evicted image?
Laura: two recovery paths: operator-approved manual rehydrate from archival seed, or fastpull from other cluster nodes if lease hasn't fully expired and blobs still exist elsewhere.
Maya: audit stream: emit `artifact.evicted` events into audit pipeline with tombstone payload and signer. Keep audit retention longer than content TTL for compliance.
Raj: compatibility with package-graph format?
Laura: minimal changes: add tombstone objects and an optional `retention` header field. Agents ignore unknown manifest fields.
Tim: +1. We should add an emergency rehydrate runbook for on-call.
Laura: action items:
- Laura: draft RFC + tombstone schema + example CLI UX (this week)
- Raj: index sharding design + compaction schedule (next week)
- Maya: audit retention + KMS signing policy doc (next week)
- Tim: emergency rehydrate playbook & runbook (next week)
Raj: can we run a staging sim that rehydrates 1k evicted artifacts to measure operator latency and fastpull success rate?
Laura: yes scheduling sim and will include perf targets in RFC.
Maya: :thumbsup:
OperatorBot: created issue RW-eviction-2026 and assigned Laura, Raj, Maya, Tim — https://go/repo/RW-eviction-2026
Tim: closing thread to reduce noise; will move discussion to the RFC PR and the new issue.
